title: Research lists, feedback, and a better look at the neighbours
items: Decade colours on the map and chart are easier to tell apart, including for colour-blind visitors (same order as before: 1880s purple, 1890s blue, 1900s green, 1910s gold, 1920s red, 1930s brown).
Fixed: with Filter by map on, the map could keep redrawing by itself after zooming (the heading above the map kept wrapping and unwrapping).

Research lists. Click ☆ Save on any permit to collect it into a named list (a walking tour, a nomination, one architect's houses) and add a note to each one. Lists in the header opens them: download a CSV, print a page with sources and notes, or copy a link that opens the list (notes included) for someone else. Very long lists are passed on as a small file instead, opened with Import list.
Send feedback in the header, and Report a problem with this permit on each permit, open a short form over the page with the permit already filled in.

Building counts: entries that spell out large numbers ("forty-two 1-story br res", "eighteen …") now show the right number of buildings; about 210 permits were overcounted. Stores, garages and other kinds of building are counted too ("three 1-story brick stores" was shown as 7). When a permit's addresses cover more house numbers than it has buildings, the permit says both, e.g. 42 buildings · 60 house numbers.
Permits for several buildings group their building buttons by the address ranges as printed, and the red ring on the main map follows the building you pick.

Photo panel: the arrows walk along the street to the next house on either side, past the ends of a range. A neighbour you show gets a blue ring and a dashed line from the permit, on both maps. Corner houses get a ▲ button for the house around the corner. A neighbour that is only known from a permit shows a short card instead of a photo, and the small map no longer jumps.
Map dot colours by decade are now easier to tell apart for colour-blind readers, and each dot's hover says its decade.
Searching an address or owner that finds a single permit opens it straight away.
Sizes with fractions ("44x99 1/2") no longer confuse the address: 684 permits were placed again.

title: Study areas, full screen and more old maps
items: Study area: draw a shape on the map and keep only the permits inside it. It can be saved with your filters, shared in a link, and exported as GeoJSON.
Full screen button: the map and permit details fill the screen, with the filters and a legend kept in view.
New map layers: the 1949–1951 Sanborn fire-insurance maps (the Loop so far) and a ca. 1930 annexations map.
Permits for several buildings say how many buildings, in the table and the permit panel; where the entry doesn't say, they show how many addresses it covers.
A search hidden by the Confidence filter now says how many matches are at Medium or Low, with a button to show them. An address with no permits says whether the address exists today.
The page scan and the enlarged Assessor photo open over the left side, so the permit stays in view.
Downloads include a confidence column (High / Medium / Low).

title: One Layers menu
items: All the maps are in one Layers menu at the bottom right: the 1892, 1906 and 1913 maps, the plat map, 2024 satellite photos, the present-day map and the permit dots. Old maps have a slider from the original to the background removed.
The map's title says how many permits are showing, how many are hidden by your filters, and has a Clear filters link.
The whole city fits on first load; selected community areas are highlighted.

title: Confidence you can see
items: Each dot shows how sure we are of its place: a solid disc (High), a disc with a hole (Medium) or a small pale dot (Low). The Confidence key explains each.
The 1906 Blanchard map is available as a layer.
Permits that print a street corner instead of a house number are placed at that corner.
A new, cleaner base map, hosted with the site.

title: Satellite view, measuring, better text
items: 2024 Cook County satellite photos as a map layer.
Measure tool for distances and lot sizes, in feet.
Every permit's text was re-read from its scan, so fewer misread names and numbers. Where a cost was hard to read, the permit says so and gives the second reading.
Condo buildings now get their Assessor photo and year built.

title: Confidence filter and phones
items: Confidence filter: only High-confidence locations show by default; tick Medium and Low to see the rest.
Phones and upright tablets get their own layout: a full-screen map, a search bar, and one pull-up panel for the list and the permit.
Pressing Enter in the address box goes straight to the address.
Architect names that differ only in spacing or periods (A.G. Lund, A G Lund, AG Lund) are treated as one.

title: Beta opens
items: The beta site opens to testers. Thank you for trying it! Please use Send feedback for anything that looks wrong or could work better.
